fields.scopeNotes: A managed vector database and retrieval layer for the claims-document assistant, the second use case after fraud detection. In scope: hosting, index management, hybrid search, access control per claims team, and EU data residency. Out of scope: the embedding model itself and the LLM, both already selected. Volume is modest by vendor standards, roughly 4 million document chunks growing 15% a year, which matters because most vendor pricing and reference architectures assume an order of magnitude more.
fields.criteriaNotes: Weighted scoring, weights published in the RFP. Each criterion is scored 1-5 against required evidence, not against the narrative. A score of 1 on any must-have is disqualifying regardless of total, which is stated up front so a strong overall score cannot carry a fatal gap. Two evaluators score independently and reconcile; the reconciliation notes are kept because that is what gets asked for if the decision is challenged.
fields.processNotes: RFI to five vendors first to filter on data residency and pricing model, then RFP to three. Four weeks for responses, a single written Q&A round published to all respondents so nobody gets a private clarification, then 90-minute technical sessions with a fixed agenda. All vendor contact goes through one named person at Nordkap procurement; direct approaches to the claims team are grounds for exclusion, which has already had to be said once.
fields.constraintNotes: Must-haves: EU-only data residency with a named region, SSO against Nordkap's existing IdP, a signed DPA covering sub-processors, and documented index export in a non-proprietary format. Deal-breakers: training on customer data by default, no way to delete a document and its embeddings on request, and per-query pricing with no cap, which makes the cost of a bad retrieval loop unbounded.
